author: SlRenderStudio
selftext: personally i think they are really high in prices and charge much as they want because enterprises pay them while users getting scraps  while quality getting degraded , like look at gemini google or chatgpt or deepseek website one they really tend to be stupid on free tiers and extremly out dated and resistant for web searching unless explicitly maximum said so . i saw this video (i am just random guy not related to creator of this [https://youtu.be/2K\_Rm8cho1I?si=rhbONqljmdE\_qnoW](https://youtu.be/2K_Rm8cho1I?si=rhbONqljmdE_qnoW) ) , if that true deepseek is getting insanely high profit margin , okay deepseek they need to recover cost of traning but why another providers it is even more expensive than deepseek when they dont even have traning costs or anything

comments.author: UncleJoesLandscaping
comments.body: The $20 subscriptions are crazy cheap. Easily worth $1000+ dollars a month in actual output if you use it well. I doubt the current pricing is sustainable for Claude or ChatGPT.

comments.author: Valdaraak
comments.body:
>i think they are really high in prices

Subscriptions are the cheapest they're ever going to be. They practically lose money on them. The reason we get "scraps" is because subscriptions are basically how they're making money off of hardware that isn't currently in use by enterprise clients. It's why usage limits constantly move around.

>deepseek is getting insanely high profit margin

There is not an AI company in the world that is making a penny of profit right now.

>why another providers it is even more expensive than deepseek

Because they're better? GPT and Claude are frontier models that blow Deepseek out of the water.

>when they dont even have traning costs or anything

You mean other providers reselling access to Deepseek or other models? Because they have to pay for the infrastructure to host and run those models, which is *insanely expensive* right now. The price isn't from the training, it's from the hardware to run the stuff.

comments.author: TheVoyant
comments.body:
You have to get into it to really get your use out of them,   
I get massive amounts of output for maybe a couple hundred bucks (my most expensive was $400, but I was testing 4 subscriptions out before I decided to go straight API)

API + Harnesses + Routing + Workflow  
Use Intelligent model 36+ on the index for the blueprint; Opus 5.5, Kimi 3.1, Astra  
Use a couple different models to review the blueprint to find holes (cost is yours decide based on scale)   
Use Cheap Coding Model in the 30s range = Deepseek, Mistral, Mimo, etc. 

I average about 1 billion in tokens used per day, though sometimes that's just one model doing a task. 

Chat GPT/Claude are getting worse and worse at the tasks, Carbon by Google might be worth it (I plan on testing it in my set up as the Intelligent model for blueprints/final reviews) 

But I'm getting game engine, dev tool kits, animation editors, the full suite of game production for a couple hundred a month and considering that one subscription of these automated services costs half that.

It's cheap imo, you just gotta be meticulous with what the deal is/best models and have zero loyalty to companies and be adaptable, as what works now, didn't in August, and what worked in August doesn't now.
